gaps.sentence: We had ___ awful weather on the crossing.
gaps.explanation: 'Weather' is uncountable — 'had awful weather', no article.

gaps.sentence: Could you pass me ___ salt, please?
gaps.explanation: 'The salt' — both speakers know which one (on the table).

gaps.sentence: It's ___ one-way street, so you can't turn left here.
gaps.explanation: 'One' starts with /w/, a consonant sound, so 'a one-way street'.

gaps.sentence: ___ rich often object to paying inheritance tax.
gaps.explanation: 'The rich' = rich people as a group.

gaps.sentence: ___ rich variety of birds lives in the Danube delta.
gaps.explanation: A rich variety of… — variety is countable here, first mention.

gaps.sentence: We had ___ wonderful time in Prague.
gaps.explanation: 'Have a wonderful/great/good time' — 'time' here is countable and takes 'a'.

gaps.sentence: She got ___ injury during the warm-up.
gaps.explanation: 'An injury' — vowel sound; 'during the warm-up' is the specific one.
'The courage he showed' — the relative clause makes it definite.
